name: store_flood
kind: which property of a GEMM epilogue's lane stores makes them cheaper than the row4 cell of v2 (lane interleaving, completion two requests later, destination not in L2); one SM; no workload-based fitting
question: v2 row4 (4 half-written sectors in 4 lines per request) costs 8.0-8.4 cycles per request on one SM, fresh or refilled. The same counts in cutlass_f16bf16_dense_tma_ws_00 cost at most 5.05-5.7. Which difference matters: (i) lanes of one request interleave the four rows (lane l on row l % 4) instead of filling them one after another, (ii) the other half of a sector arrives two requests later, alternating between two row sets, (iii) the destination has never been written (not resident in L2), (iv) none of these?
probe: store_flood.cu extended, one SM, W in {4, 8} (W = 4 is the kernel's case), window and stamps as v1 / v2. Geometries, all width 2 (STG.E.U16), 64 B per request in 4 half sectors of 4 lines: row4 (v2 reference: lanes 8 j .. 8 j + 7 on row j, rows 4 KiB apart, fresh rows per request); epi = the kernel's pattern: lane l writes 2 B at offset 2 (l / 4) + 16 h of row s + 2 (l % 4) of the warp's current block of 8 rows (rows 8 KiB apart), request k of a warp has s = k % 2 (row set) and h = (k / 2) % 2 (half); every 4 requests complete one sector in each of the 8 rows of a block and the warp moves to its next block of 8 rows (4 blocks = 32 rows per warp), and after 16 requests it returns to the first block with the byte offset along the rows advanced by 32 (the order read from the kernel's sector masks: +0 / +8192 / +0 / +8192, then +65536 ..; 384 requests write 32 rows x 768 B; each warp its own rows); lace = row4 with interleaved lanes only (lane l on row l % 4, offset 2 (l / 4), fresh rows per request, rows 4 KiB apart); epi_seq = epi with lanes filling the rows one after another (lanes 8 j .. 8 j + 7 on row s + 2 j) - completion order of epi without the interleave. Destination modes: warm = host memset before every launch (v1 / v2); virgin = a fresh allocation per launch that the host never writes, every address written once per launch (repetitions use disjoint parts). Cells: {row4, epi, lace, epi_seq} x {warm, virgin} x W {4, 8}; control none. Runs a and b, 8 launches x 17 repetitions (repetition 0 discarded).

controls.sass: as v2 (49 clock reads, 8 STG.E.U16 between neighbours, nothing else in the window).
controls.timing: row4 warm W = 4 reproduces v2 (8.36) within 5 %; runs a and b within 5 %.
controls.geometry: the model script recomputes sectors, lines, half-written sectors and lane-order line switches per request from the cell definition and prints them (all cells: 4 sectors, 4 lines, 4 half-written; switches 4 for row4 / epi_seq, 32 for epi / lace).

derivation: T = (steady group gap - control) / 8 / W per cell.

predictions_before_data.v1_rule: sectors + partly written lines = 8.0 in every cell (the rule of v1 knows none of the differences).
predictions_before_data.kernel_bound: at least one of the epi cells at W = 4 reads <= 5.7.
predictions_before_data.if_interleave: epi and lace <= 5.7, epi_seq and row4 about 8.
predictions_before_data.if_completion: epi and epi_seq <= 5.7, lace and row4 about 8.
predictions_before_data.if_l2: virgin cells <= 5.7 where the warm ones read 8.

outcomes_before_data.found: If exactly one factor separates the cells as in one of the three if_ lines (the cheap cells within 15 % of each other, the others within 10 % of 8): an addendum states the rule in terms of that factor (what a request must look like to pay the partly-written-line extra) and the engine fact it needs; the partial-line leaf is then installed with that condition. A second run with the factor varied (e.g. interleave of 2 rows, completion distance 1 / 2 / 4) is declared in that addendum if the form is not determined.
outcomes_before_data.mixed: If two factors each lower the cost: report both, addendum before install.
outcomes_before_data.none: If every cell reads about 8: the kernel bound is not explained by the store pattern; the epilogue of that kernel is re-attributed (stores may not be the binding resource there).

prediction_check: H100 replay of epi and row4 (warm, W = 4) with the installed rule: T within 15 %; then the full-gpu 500 x 2 regression against main's baseline (fg-over20/full-h1).
not_allowed: No family / case / shape specific timing: the epi geometry is taken from a kernel's sector masks to reproduce a store pattern, the rule must be stated in terms of the request (lanes, sectors, lines, completion), not of the kernel. No tuning to the full-gpu error; post-data changes of a criterion are labelled.

addenda.text: epi definition corrected against the kernel's sector masks: after the four requests that complete a sector in each of 8 rows the kernel moves on to the next 8 rows and only returns to a line 16 requests later; the first wording kept the warp on the same 8 rows. epi_seq follows the same order.

addenda.runs: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/store_flood/{h100-v3r2,b300-v3r2} (table.txt; geometry self-check 4 / 4 / 4 and 4 / 32 / 32 / 4 lane runs as declared; v3r1 are failed builds)
addenda.text: T in cycles per request at W = 4 (W = 8 in brackets). h100: row4 8.38 warm / 8.19 virgin (7.8 / 8.0), lace 8.38 / 8.19, epi 8.59 / 8.59 (7.7), epi_seq 8.59 / 8.59. b300: row4 7.86 / 7.45 (6.5 / 6.3), lace 7.83 / 7.48, epi 7.31 / 7.31 (6.0 / 5.9), epi_seq 7.31 / 7.31. Prediction v1_rule (8.0 everywhere) holds on h100 within 7 %; prediction kernel_bound (some epi cell <= 5.7) FAILED. Outcome 'none' as declared: lane interleaving, the completion order of the kernel and the L2 presence of the destination do not change what a saturated SM needs per request. The kernel readings were then recomputed over all STG PCs (PC sampling, $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/pcs): the same request shape with four epilogue warps costs 17.3 warp-cycles per STG in cutlass_f16bf16_dense_tma_ws_00 (4.3 cycles per request at SM level), 31.7 in cutlass_f16bf16_dense_tma_ws_06 (7.9) and 51.6 in cutlass_dense_cpasync_00 (12.9). The per-request cost in kernels is therefore not a function of the request alone, and the first kernel runs at half of what this probe measures for the same stream on a saturated SM, with every SM of the card storing. Not explained. Nothing installed; the partly-written-line leaf stays 0. Next measurement (declared here): the kernel's own binary with one tile (one CTA on one SM) and with one tile per SM, cycles and PC sampling of the store region, against the 1024-tile case - it separates 'the SM serves this code faster than the probe stream' from 'the probe's steady state is not the kernel's regime'.

addenda.when: 2026-11-14, after the kernel runs with 1 / 66 / 132 tiles, the second B300 unit and the bridge cells (data seen)
addenda.text: (1) The kernels' own binaries alone on the card (hopper dense_algorithms, 128 x 128 tiles, 512 STG.E.U16 per tile from 4 warps; ncu + PC sampling, $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/hw/{epi,cpa}, reader fg-over20/tools/epi_scale.py), cycles per request at SM level over the store region: f16_nt_tma: 5.2 with one tile on the card, 9.6 with one tile on each of 132 SMs, 5.0 in the 1024-tile case; f16_nt_cpasync: 13.7 / 19.6 / 12.7 (the STG instruction alone 8.6 with one tile, lg_throttle; its stores alternate with LDL stack reloads). The engine reproduces the one-tile tma kernel (store region 2491 against 2394 cycles per warp; whole kernel 1.05) and the one-tile cpasync kernel only in total (1.00; STG 483 against 1477 cycles per warp, compensated by over-waits elsewhere). (2) v1 rerun on a second B300 unit (b300-r2, GPU-826a4f53): identical to b300-r1 (w4.s128.l32 T = 31.9). The B300 conflict of the v2 addendum is therefore not a unit difference: on B300 the same request (32 part-written sectors in 32 lines) costs 31.9 in the v1 kernel and 62.0 in the v2 grid kernel. (3) Bridge cells on the epi stream, h100, W = 4 ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/store_flood/h100-bridge-r6; not declared in a protocol beforehand, exploratory): none 8.66, no fence and a single window 8.66, 128-request window 8.61, per-lane data 8.19, arithmetic between the stores (FADD, FMUL, F2FP, ISETP, SEL per store) 7.88, all together 7.12 (512 requests in 3604 cycles; the kernel needs about 2400-2650); a predicated store could not be produced (ptxas emits a branch). Reading: the extra cycle per partly written line is a regime of the SM store path, present in every h100 probe kernel, in the B300 grid kernel and in the cpasync kernel, absent in the B300 v1 kernel and in the tma kernel; the request's sectors, lines, lane order, completion order, the destination's L2 state, fences, window length and filler arithmetic do not select it. What selects it is not known. Nothing is installed; the leaf stays 0 (the regime of the tma kernel and of the B300 v1 kernel). Next step (to be declared as protocol v4 before it is run): bisect the B300 v1 and v2 kernels, which differ only in how the CTA is launched and synchronized (grid of one CTA per SM with large dynamic shared memory, arrival polling on a global counter, slice addressing) and are both in one binary.
